packages.title: Approve concrete workspace and state presentations

Every task is chosen explicitly and all old/new drafts and source versions remain reachable.
testFocus: Primary browser history/draft/input cases, mobile layout and keyboard actions; direct text-to-video never silently becomes picture generation.

architectureDecisions.title: One new project identity, explicit legacy origins
architectureDecisions.decision: Add creation_projects with owner/revision and conversation/draft/media/edit subcollections. Map each legacy session or Studio project through an explicit origin record; never join by title, prompt or timestamp. Legacy readers remain. Adoption uses a dry-run manifest and revision-checked writer switch, not bulk rewriting of old records.

architectureDecisions.title: One acceptance authority, native executors retain their own duties
architectureDecisions.decision: Extend RequestIdempotencyService and its bindings rather than opening a second acceptance ledger. New creation_requests own immutable intent, fixed slots and aggregate outcomes. Existing video_jobs and provider/Studio attempts own actual execution facts. A unique request+slot native-executor mapping and versioned observations connect them. The outbox cannot dispatch until receipt/reservation/consumed-draft facts commit.

architectureDecisions.title: Independent execution drafts and exact history
architectureDecisions.decision: Creation, assistance, export settings, imports and Sketch acceptance each have their own execution-draft identity. Their contextual media/editor/draft IDs remain inputs. Media versions and exports are immutable; branch context is stored at acceptance. UI selection, provider completion and project preference cannot rewrite those references.

architectureDecisions.title: Separate state groups without one collection per group
architectureDecisions.decision: Connection, playback and viewer state are local. Draft save acknowledgments are owner-scoped and revisioned. Request outcome, attempt evidence, cancellation, delivery and usage are separate facts on their appropriate records. The 22 control groups are not 22 database tables or another global state enum.

architectureDecisions.title: Delivery extends existing media ownership
architectureDecisions.decision: Retain owned-media/storage/admission/grant boundaries. Generalize destination through typed legacy-session, project and owner-recovery adapters. A version becomes deliverable only after verified storage plus authoritative association. Copy creates a new association; repair never changes the original destination or invokes generation.

architectureDecisions.title: Provider capability evidence controls recovery
architectureDecisions.decision: Every offered provider action must declare external start/status/cancel/result support and captured deadlines. Persist external operation identity and request hash before treating a later browser/worker event as recoverable. When status/cancel is unavailable, expose unable/unknown/needs-attention; do not invent support or retry uncertain generation.

architectureDecisions.title: Deterministic video editing and isolated export
architectureDecisions.decision: Add shared/video-edit pure commands/validation and a versioned render manifest. Use exact 30 fps frame intervals and 48 kHz samples, fixed initial presets and bundled typography. A dedicated pinned FFmpeg renderer uses bounded local inputs and a private Cloud Run task service with Firestore outbox/Cloud Tasks; it is not a generation provider or the API service at concurrency 80. See the export research for exact proposed limits and qualification gates.

architectureDecisions.title: New customer ledger, preserved existing obligations
architectureDecisions.decision: New usage/entitlement records own quotes, per-slot reservations/settlement and new purchases. Existing Studio/Sketch provider budgets and legacy refund ledger remain separate. Paid mode stays disabled until server enforcement, production offer configuration and hosted acceptance are complete. Text help/Sketch retain the current bounded free semantics specified by the contract. New v2 provider executor jobs keep native creditsReserved=0 even when their canonical request has a paid usage reservation. Native refund compatibility must never refund or settle v2 customer usage; the canonical request/slot ledger alone does that. The UI reads canonical usage rather than interpreting a native zero-credit field as a free customer request.

architectureDecisions.title: Hosted checkout and deterministic grants
architectureDecisions.decision: Use provider-hosted checkout rather than a custom checkout UI. A verified paid invoice/purchase identity grants allowance exactly once; redirects and duplicate/out-of-order webhook deliveries cannot grant it. Initial offer has explicit monthly allowance and manual usage purchases only. Cancellation/past-due stops new grants/admission when paid access ends, while captured accepted reservations and owned results remain recoverable. Exact price/allowance/expiry policy is immutable release configuration, not an inferred legacy credit value.

architectureDecisions.title: Feature routing and rollback preserve new data
architectureDecisions.decision: New project writes are server-gated. Once a legacy origin activates the new writer, stale legacy writes are refused. Rollback disables admission and uses retained v2 read/recovery UI; it does not squeeze new records into old prompt shapes. Existing refunds/attachments/in-flight outcome observation remain operational.

architectureDecisions.title: Adoption fences new authoring, not previously accepted completion
architectureDecisions.decision: Adoption first commits a source writer epoch/fence that every legacy authoring/intake transaction checks. New legacy authoring and acceptance stop; existing accepted native jobs/turns/admission debts are inventoried under their immutable owner/receipt/native IDs and original destinations. Only allowlisted completion/attachment/refund operations may continue. Their new versions/checkpoints project into the adopted project once using native ID+slot/version keys and a durable cursor/outbox; already copied results deduplicate. Do not trust caller timestamps to claim pre-fence acceptance. Unknown or untraceable in-flight legacy work blocks activation until drained or explicitly resolved; it is never guessed or silently cancelled. Existing charged refund debt keeps its original ledger. Rollback retains the allowlist, projector and canonical read/recovery authority. The completion exception is an internal executor/repair authority: a browser cannot claim it by sending a native ID or purpose flag. Verify the stored receipt/attempt/output binding on every permitted completion.

architectureDecisions.title: Legacy public links require evidence-based binding
architectureDecisions.decision: Old ShareRecord lacks owner/project/version fields. Bind a legacy link only when authoritative owned-media/version records establish exactly one immutable origin and owner for its storage object; do not infer from prompt, description, title or time. Store the binding/revocation gate before serving it through the new resolver. Zero/multiple possible origins or unverifiable immutable bytes leave the old link unavailable with generic public copy; an authenticated proven owner may explicitly publish a new link from a selected version. Never silently choose a project. Thus saved owned media and uniquely verifiable links survive; preserving every ambiguous old public link is not a promise. Project trash/revocation/rollback must continue to deny bound links, and restoring a project never republishes them.

architectureDecisions.title: Normalization and renderer version are executable identities
architectureDecisions.decision: WP-21 owns probe/normalized preview proxy creation, cache and cleanup bounds as well as exports. Keys include exact source version/object generation/checksum, normalization version and required decoder/renderer fingerprint; customer-owned originals never change. Accepted exports route to the exact recorded renderer implementation/image digest. Deploying B does not execute A requests under B; retain A routing until its requests/recovery close or report that exact implementation unavailable. Proxy failure pauses preview media time without letting captions/audio drift; it does not imply the source generation failed.

definitionOfDone: Required contract states/events have real application boundary tests, including default rejections with no provider/process/usage side effects.
Each assigned acceptance ID is exercised with its original Given/When/Then; fixture-only model traces are not application tests.
Existing ownership/receipt/media/refund tests stay. Contradicted old workflow assertions change only in the package implementing the replacement behavior.
Auth, authorization, payment and user-data behavior includes a negative path. Transactional uniqueness/CAS/settlement passes the actual Firestore-emulator race profile without skips.

Every commit passes root typecheck, quiet ESLint, architecture, unit and replay gates. Shared-contract changes typecheck immediately; registration/lifecycle changes add bootstrap and DI; route/catalog/flag changes add drift checks.
Before handoff, lint including CSS, build and relevant provider-free browser journeys pass. The required renderer profile runs the real pinned FFmpeg image and checks bytes/frames/audio.
New UI composition has linked approved designs and browser/accessibility evidence; old Page 21 styling is retained unless explicitly replaced.
Rollback, saved-record compatibility and outstanding recovery obligations are proved before retiring a route/writer.
No required missing environment, provider cancellation/status capability, live creative quality, pricing data or hosted rollout evidence is silently marked passed.
Add executable tests with the behavior change; unimplemented cases stay in this plan, not as skipped/TODO passing application tests. Whole-case closure waits for every required boundary/profile.

State/event fixtures satisfy every unrelated schema/auth/input/quote prerequisite and demonstrate reaching the owning command/observer. An earlier malformed-payload rejection cannot substitute for the intended state-specific rejection. Assert its specific error/outcome and unchanged effects.

releaseGates.condition: Use the existing behavior contract/state cases to begin design now. Concrete state presentations and linked new frames must be reviewed before new UI implementation; schema and harness implementation do not block design. Retain existing Page 21 styling.
Actual transactional CAS/admission/usage races pass against Firestore emulator. Skips fail this gate.
releaseGates.evidence: Emulator test report with exact source revision and conflicting-call histories.

releaseGates.condition: Real render fixture/container/resource checks and browser preview parity pass for every enabled preset.
releaseGates.evidence: Pinned image/font/manifest hashes, ffprobe/decode/frame/audio assertions and browser artifacts.

releaseGates.condition: All state/transition/rejection owners, all 137 original acceptance cases, actor adapters and supplemental cases assigned to G-APP have passing application evidence. Hosted/activation supplements remain separate named gates.
Separately authorized bounded provider quality/cost and staged worker/IAM/recovery/rollback proof qualify the actual offered actions. Current old test spend is not a new allowance.
releaseGates.evidence: Per-offer output/revision/recovery/cost evidence and staging results; source/catalog data alone is insufficient.

releaseGates.condition: Reviewed production prices, customer allocations/expiry policy, provider budgets, recovery/render limits and support policies; verified paid grants and no-redebit behavior.
releaseGates.evidence: Versioned production offer manifest plus authorized release record.

releaseGates.condition: Clean migration dry run and counts/identity samples; explicit execution authorization before production adoption; post-run verification.
releaseGates.evidence: Exact adoption manifest, permission record, before/after identities and rollback rehearsal.

supplementalCases.given: A malformed new request and a valid legacy saved take exist.
supplementalCases.then: Reject unknown/new-write violations while legacy remains readable; unresolved pending input cannot enter accepted request.

supplementalCases.given: Another process occupies the default browser test port.
supplementalCases.then: Allocate/configure a separate URL and preserve the existing process; test artifacts remain run-scoped.

supplementalCases.given: Controlled fixtures attempt an unexpected external provider request.
supplementalCases.then: Outbound guard fails the test; no paid call escapes and no replay is mislabeled live proof.

supplementalCases.given: Text contains unsupported glyph, missing font or overflow.

supplementalCases.given: Source path/URL/filter syntax is supplied by a hostile client.

supplementalCases.given: GCS object creation succeeds but acknowledgment is lost.

supplementalCases.given: A renderer loses its lease and later attempts publication.
supplementalCases.when: A new observer reconciles the same attempt.
supplementalCases.then: Fencing prevents stale publication; no blind rerender; durable output is recovered or loss is explicit.

supplementalCases.given: Renderer reaches memory/scratch/time limits or receives shutdown.
supplementalCases.when: Run the actual pinned container fixture.
supplementalCases.then: Stop bounded work, retain evidence, publish no partial file, and enter the specified failure/recovery state.

supplementalCases.given: An outbox event/task is delivered twice or a dispatcher dies after enqueue.
supplementalCases.then: One native export attempt/claim is authoritative; pending outbox/reconciliation remains discoverable and no charge repeats.

supplementalCases.given: A checkout return URL claims success but no verified invoice/purchase exists.
supplementalCases.then: No allowance is granted; new paid work remains blocked until authoritative entitlement exists.

supplementalCases.given: Same paid invoice arrives in duplicate and different webhook events, out of order.
supplementalCases.then: Exactly one grant per business billing identity; older events cannot reverse newer paid-access facts.

supplementalCases.given: A forged signature or another owner's customer/purchase ID is submitted.
supplementalCases.then: Reject it without altering either owner's entitlement or revealing private billing data.

supplementalCases.given: Hosted checkout is cancelled or payment fails; alternatively the paid period ends.
supplementalCases.then: No false success/grant; old work stays readable and already accepted reservations retain their captured policy.

supplementalCases.given: Legacy sessions/Studio projects have equal names, missing history and saved URLs.
supplementalCases.when: Run adoption twice on isolated copies.
supplementalCases.then: Stable explicit-origin mapping, unchanged original IDs/bytes, no guessed history and no duplicate projects.

supplementalCases.given: A legacy tab saves after new-writer activation and another v2 edit has landed.
supplementalCases.then: Server refuses stale authority; no mixed writer overwrites v2 work.

supplementalCases.given: A newly adopted project has v2 drafts, jobs and outputs.
supplementalCases.then: All v2 records and recovery remain readable; no lossy reverse migration, duplicate dispatch or revived public share.

supplementalCases.given: Project contains still revisions, a running alternative and an unfinished composition.
supplementalCases.when: Finish/reopen/edit an image, a usable shot and a final video amid failures.
supplementalCases.then: All three deliverables survive, exact old-version edits work and no unrelated draft/focus/inputs are overwritten.

supplementalCases.given: Staged release has accepted running requests and active purchases.
supplementalCases.then: New spending stops; receipts, recovery, releases/refunds, existing owned downloads and work access remain available.

supplementalCases.given: The renderer service is private and queue/outbox/IAM permissions are deployed.
supplementalCases.when: Try unauthenticated/wrong-task invocations and interrupt task delivery.
supplementalCases.then: Unauthorized calls fail; authorized exact tasks reconcile correctly; local/emulator success is not substituted for this hosted evidence.

supplementalCases.given: A new canonical request reserves paid customer usage while a charged legacy job still exists.
supplementalCases.when: Execute, fail/recover and settle both paths.
supplementalCases.then: New native executor jobs retain creditsReserved=0 and use only the v2 usage ledger; old positive-credit jobs still require the legacy refunder. Neither ledger charges/refunds the other request.

supplementalCases.given: A legacy queued/running video and a partially running Studio batch were accepted before the adoption writer fence.
supplementalCases.when: Activate the new writer while both complete; then exercise rollback.
supplementalCases.then: Only allowlisted native completion writes continue to their original destinations; every late slot/result projects once into canonical history with the same original receipt/native/source IDs.

supplementalCases.given: A legacy picture/clip has pending attachment repair and an older charged job has refund debt before adoption.
supplementalCases.then: Keep original media/destination/ledger IDs, permit only the authorized debt operations, project media once and never run another generation or move old refund debt into the v2 ledger.

supplementalCases.given: A legacy caller races adoption preparation or an in-flight operation has no provable immutable acceptance identity.
supplementalCases.then: Authoring-epoch transaction admits at most one side of the race. Untraceable work blocks activation until resolved; no timestamp guess, silent cancellation or stranded result.

supplementalCases.given: Old links have respectively one, zero and multiple provable source owner/project/version candidates.
supplementalCases.when: Resolve/bind links, trash/restore the source project, then roll back the new UI.
supplementalCases.then: Only the uniquely verified binding can serve; missing/ambiguous links remain unavailable and may be explicitly republished by a proven owner. Trash/revocation denial persists across restore/rollback.

supplementalCases.given: VFR source has a normalized proxy keyed to source/normalization fingerprints.
supplementalCases.when: Preview/export it, then lose/buffer the proxy and resume.
supplementalCases.then: Frame anchors match the pinned normalization; media time, captions and audio pause/resume together. A missing proxy has its own recovery state and does not mark source generation failed.

supplementalCases.given: Export X was accepted under renderer image A and normalization N.
supplementalCases.when: Deploy B before X starts or recovers.
supplementalCases.then: Dispatch/recovery selects A/N or reports it unavailable; never silently use B or change the accepted output plan. New exports may explicitly use B.

supplementalCases.given: Acceptance/outbox commit succeeds and the API/dispatcher dies before task creation; no browser returns.
supplementalCases.then: Enqueue/reconcile the original request or reach its captured Needs attention deadline. Execution cannot begin until its recovery obligation is durable.

supplementalCases.given: Fixed lossless fixtures exercise cuts/crops/captions and AAC-aligned audio impulses.
supplementalCases.when: Run preview/export parity for each supported browser/preset.
supplementalCases.then: Pass the numerical renderProfile tolerances including zero frame/crop error and exact pre-encode overlays; no automatic threshold blessing or false container-duration equality.

Planned suite paths are not existing tests or passing evidence.

renderProfile.qualification: SUP-06 through SUP-14 plus SUP-24; reduce profile rather than silently exceed bounds if the actual image cannot pass.

parityTolerance.evaluation: Fixed lossless numbered/color/text/audio fixtures, same pinned renderer/decoder/normalization, BT.709 SDR. Compare browser content at exact media timestamps against server references; exclude UI chrome. AAC encoder priming/padding is measured and aligned, not hidden by relaxing frame/cue timing. If a supported browser cannot pass, block that profile and fix it; changing a threshold requires a reviewed contract change, not automatic blessing.
